answers.how: The cat moves about 194 px in 2.042 s, giving a scale of 0.00752 m/px. The chalkboard is about 197 px tall.
The chair spans about 90 px horizontally; multiplying by the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px gives its width.
The teacher's table spans about 320 px horizontally, using the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px.
The back-wall ceiling-to-floor extent is about 346 px, using the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px.
A local fit to airplane positions around 1 s gives velocity components of approximately 729 and 36 px/s, converted using 0.00752 m/px.
A local quadratic fit around 1 s gives airplane acceleration components of approximately -380 and 1060 px/s²; their magnitude is converted using 0.00752 m/px.
Tracking the airplane around 1.25 s gives velocity components of approximately 609 and 213 px/s, converted using 0.00752 m/px.
A local quadratic fit around 1.25 s gives acceleration components of approximately -650 and 570 px/s², converted using 0.00752 m/px.
In frame 0, the cat's horizontal extent including its tail is about 89 px, using the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px.
The cat extends about 65 px vertically from its raised tail to its paws, using 0.00752 m/px.
The chalkboard's outer horizontal extent is about 611 px, using the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px.
The clock's outer diameter is about 51 px, using the cat-derived scale of 0.00752 m/px.
